question: Failure to pass meconium within 48 hours of birth in a term neonate is abnormal and requires evaluation to exclude Hirschsprung's disease, anal atresia, or meconium ileus (in cystic fibrosis).

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: Incorrect. The statement is TRUE. Delayed first passage of meconium (>48 hours) is abnormal in a term neonate and is a recognised surgical red flag. Hirschsprung's disease and anorectal malformations are the two most important diagnoses to exclude. Every newborn examination MUST include inspection of the anus to exclude imperforate anus before any first feeding.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct! 95% of term neonates pass meconium within the first 24 hours; virtually all by 48 hours. Failure to pass meconium by 48 hours is one of the five neonatal surgical red flags and mandates evaluation. Causes: Hirschsprung's disease (aganglionic segment), imperforate anus (detected on newborn examination), meconium ileus/plug syndrome (cystic fibrosis association), or functional immotility in preterm neonates. Examine the anus visually on every newborn.
